humanized_findings.plain_english_action: Place a strong on-brand photo (a tuned WRX/STI or Focus RS, or installed parts) behind the vehicle selector.

humanized_findings.plain_english_action: Keep this blue as your action color and reuse it for any new primary button.

humanized_findings.plain_english_action: Add a short trust strip below the hero with a guarantee, easy returns, a real customers-served figure, and a support number.

humanized_findings.plain_english_action: Keep these logos, and repeat the strongest ones near the pay button when you build out checkout.

humanized_findings.plain_english_action: Rewrite the title to lead with what you sell and which cars it fits, then your brand once at the end.
humanized_findings.plain_english_summary: Your homepage's browser/search title is just 'AWDMods – AWDMods' — your brand name twice, with no mention of the parts or the cars you fit. humanized_findings.plain_english_action: Write a one-sentence description (about 150 characters) naming your catalog and the vehicles you cover.
humanized_findings.plain_english_summary: Your homepage has no meta description, so Google builds the search snippet from whatever scraps it can find on a page that's mostly menus and product thumbnails. You have no control over how your most important page is summarized in search results.

notes: Single-shot synthesis. The two LCP/preload findings and the two CLS findings were surfaced once per device and carry distinct per-device canonical references (performance-ux F-37/F-76 and F-24/F-17); each renders into its own device document only and is not a cross-device synchronized ref.

Only content-seo F-32 (title tag) and the ADJACENT ethics F-16 (privacy-policy staging-domain link) are rendered byte-identically into both audit documents; all other page-level findings were caught by a single device's review and render into that one document.
Seven CLEAR ethics findings are not rendered (default rendering skips CLEAR); the Ethics Gate section lists only the single ADJACENT finding.

priority_path.narrative: The single most valuable screen on the site is doing almost no selling. On desktop the band from the navigation row down to the category tiles is a flat black void whose only occupants are four Make/Model/Year/Trim dropdowns floating at y=308 and a 59x59px magnifier button; on mobile the same hero offers no headline and pushes the FIND PARTS button below the fold. There is no headline, value statement, product, or supporting image, so a first-time visitor scanning the top-left in the natural F-pattern cannot answer what AWDMods sells or why to buy here. The de-facto primary action, the Find parts submit, is an unlabeled search icon that visually duplicates the separate top-of-page site search, so the main conversion control reads as a generic search affordance rather than a commit button. Add a concrete headline above the selector naming the offer and the cars, set an on-brand hero image behind the selector to fill the void, pull the category tiles up so they sit above the fold, and render the submit as a full, solid, labeled "Find My Parts" button. These are template-level edits to the hero section; no backend work is required.
priority_path.title: Fill the empty above-fold band with a headline, hero media, and a labeled primary button

priority_path.narrative: The Featured Collection grid lists named products with brands, live prices, and visible 5.0-star ratings with counts, yet the page exposes none of this in structured data. The only JSON-LD blocks in the head are OnlineStore and WebSite, so the stars a shopper can see cannot become rich-result stars in Google, and AI shopping agents have no machine-readable product data to match or recommend. A controlled test attributed roughly a 20% organic-traffic uplift to review schema alone. Add ItemList JSON-LD wrapping each featured product as a Product with offers (price, priceCurrency, availability, url) and AggregateRating (ratingValue, ratingCount) drawn from the same fields already rendered on the cards, render it server-side, and validate with Google's Rich Results Test. AggregateRating values must mirror the real review data shown on the cards.
priority_path.title: Add Product and AggregateRating structured data to the rated, priced featured products

priority_path.narrative: Across the Featured Collection, prices render as a single bare number with no MSRP strikethrough, no compare-at, and no installment framing on items well over $1,000. The Borla exhaust card on the same row proves the theme already supports a reference price: it shows FROM $1,649.99 over a struck-through $1,847.99. So the capability exists and is used on exactly one of eight cards, which teaches shoppers to expect an anchor and then withholds it everywhere else, and the lone discount reads as arbitrary. On mobile the $135.99 floor-mat set is judged against a neighboring $49 card and reads as the expensive option rather than the premium one. Populate the compare-at field on discounted SKUs so the theme renders the struck-through reference price uniformly, lead higher-ticket items with the saving stated explicitly, and surface a Shop Pay Installments or Affirm line beneath each live price for items roughly $150 and up — the store already supports Shop Pay, its mark is in the footer payment row. A four-figure exhaust reads very differently as a bare number versus "$1,847.99 to $1,766.00, as low as $147/mo."
priority_path.title: Anchor every featured price with a reference price and an installment line

priority_path.narrative: Four of the highest-confidence findings resolve with copy or HTML-attribute edits inside the theme head and the product-card component. The title is AWDMods - AWDMods, the brand name duplicated at 17 characters with no category or fitment keyword; there is no meta description (the only fallback is the single word AWDMods); the head requests a large-image social card but supplies no og:image to fill it; and every product image carries its CSS class list as alt text instead of a description. Titles under 30 characters are rewritten by Google more than 95% of the time. Rewrite the title to front-load the offer and the cars, add a ~150-character meta description and matching og:description, add a 1200x630 og:image, and set each product image's alt from the product title at the card component level. None require new infrastructure or design review.
priority_path.title: Rewrite the head: descriptive title, meta description, Open Graph image, and real image alt text

priority_path.narrative: The homepage answers what you sell but never answers why to trust you. The only above-fold trust-adjacent element is the free-shipping bar, which speaks to delivery cost, not credibility; there is no guarantee, returns promise, customer count, press mention, or aggregate-rating figure anywhere on the page, and on mobile no reassurance sits near the Made-to-Order products where the "what if it doesn't fit my car" question forms. Compounding this, most featured cards carry zero reviews, and the cards that do rate show a flawless 5.0 on just two or three reviews — a perfect average on a tiny count reads as too good to be true rather than reassuring. Add a compact trust strip below the hero (guarantee, easy returns, a real customers-served or aggregate-rating figure, a visible support number) plus a one-line returns reassurance near the product cards, keep collecting reviews from every buyer so featured products cross five reviews and the average settles into the trusted 4.0-4.7 band, and prefer featuring products that already carry reviews so the grid leads with proof instead of bare prices.
priority_path.title: Add a trust block below the hero and stop shipping reviewless featured products
